    Naive and delay-adjusted case fatality ratio

    Source: R/outbreak-delays.R
    epi_cfr.Rd

    During an outbreak, dividing deaths by cases underestimates the case fatality ratio (CFR), because many recent cases have not yet had time to die. The delay-adjusted estimator of Nishiura et al. (2009) divides deaths by the expected number of cases with a known outcome, given the distribution of the delay from onset (or report) to death, as in the cfr package. Intervals are likelihood-ratio intervals from a binomial likelihood in which the cases with known outcomes are the trials.

    Usage

    epi_cfr(
  .data,
  cases,
  deaths,
  delay = NULL,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  cumulative = FALSE
)

    Arguments

    .data

    A data frame in date order with equally spaced rows (days).

    cases

    Daily cases.

    deaths

    Daily deaths.

    delay

    Probabilities of the delay from case to death, starting at a delay of 0 days, such as the probability column of epi_delay_pmf(). NULL gives only the naive estimate.

    conf_level

    Confidence level.

    cumulative

    If TRUE, returns the estimate using the data up to each row (to watch the estimate settle), added to .data.

    Value

    A tibble with method ("naive" and "delay_adjusted"), deaths, cases, known_outcomes, cfr, lower and upper; with cumulative = TRUE, .data with cfr_naive, cfr_adjusted, cfr_lower and cfr_upper (for the adjusted estimate).

    References

    Nishiura, H., Klinkenberg, D., Roberts, M. and Heesterbeek, J. A. P. (2009). Early epidemiological assessment of the virulence of emerging infectious diseases: a case study of an influenza pandemic. PLOS ONE, 4, e6852. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0006852

    Linton, N. M., Kobayashi, T., Yang, Y., Hayashi, K., Akhmetzhanov, A. R., Jung, S., Yuan, B., Kinoshita, R. and Nishiura, H. (2020). Incubation period and other epidemiological characteristics of 2019 novel coronavirus infections with right truncation. Journal of Clinical Medicine, 9, 538. doi:10.3390/jcm9020538

    Examples

    # Onset-to-death delay for COVID-19: lognormal, mean 20.2 days, SD 11.6
# (Linton et al. 2020)
sdlog <- sqrt(log(1 + (11.6 / 20.2)^2))
meanlog <- log(20.2) - sdlog^2 / 2
pmf <- diff(plnorm(0:61, meanlog, sdlog))
epi_cfr(nz_covid_outcomes_2020, cases, deaths, delay = pmf / sum(pmf))
#> # A tibble: 2 × 7
#>   method         deaths cases known_outcomes    cfr   lower  upper
#>   <chr>           <int> <int>          <dbl>  <dbl>   <dbl>  <dbl>
#> 1 naive              23  1530          1530  0.0150 0.00972 0.0220
#> 2 delay_adjusted     23  1530          1509. 0.0152 0.00986 0.0223

early <- nz_covid_outcomes_2020[1:50, ]
epi_cfr(early, cases, deaths, delay = pmf / sum(pmf))
#> # A tibble: 2 × 7
#>   method         deaths cases known_outcomes     cfr   lower  upper
#>   <chr>           <int> <int>          <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>  <dbl>
#> 1 naive              12  1386          1386  0.00866 0.00465 0.0145
#> 2 delay_adjusted     12  1386           528. 0.0227  0.0122  0.0378
